comparator.name: Business Analytics
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027; adopted TER and exact annual catalogue, checked2026-10-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 regulations list 150 EC of compulsory named modules across three years and an open 30-EC third-year academic elective period. The 0-EC English Language Test is excluded from credit totals. The 30-EC period may be an allowed minor or approved individual courses; it is kept open here rather than filled with invented content. There is no formal bachelor specialisation. The 12-EC collaborative Bachelor Project: Business Case is the capstone and requires at least 120 EC plus prior passes in Statistical Data Analysis and Project Big Data. VU has a deeper, required calculus, operations research, programming, statistics and project sequence than UCR. The full-time English 2026–2027 pathway contains 150 EC of compulsory named study and a 30 EC open academic elective/minor period: 60 EC in each year. There is no formal specialization. The adopted regulations and exact annual XB_0112 catalogue require Data Engineering; the recruitment page’s Business Intelligence and Analytics label does not replace that unit. Bachelor Project: Business Case is one 12 EC unit including Study and Career in period 4, Academic Writing in English in period 5 and the company case in periods 5–6. Entry is assessed after December results and requires at least 120 EC, Statistical Data Analysis and Project Big Data. All third-year students take Study and Career; it must be passed before the company case starts. Academic Writing must also be passed before the project grade is awarded. Study and Career requires attendance, assignments, participation and an interview presentation, with compensatory work for notified absence. Writing requires a passed introduction, peer feedback, assignments and attendance at least five of six sessions including both feedback sessions. Teams of at most five submit a joint report/thesis and final product; each student is assessed through observed work, peer reviews, self-reflection and an individual interview. Assessment weights are analytics 20%, synthesis 20%, creativity 15%, initiative 10%, social skills 15%, presentation 10% and writing 10%. The kickoff, project-management workshop, company visit, four presentations and final company presentation are compulsory; workload is at least ten hours weekly in period 5 and full-time in period 6. Thesis and Placement Regulations apply. The English diagnostic test and required refresher are noncredit. First-year BSA normally requires 42 EC, subject to exceptions. Individual open choices need prior examination-board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100; eligible university/listed minors are exempt. The university Data Science minor is excluded for Business Analytics students; the specified Business Analytics and Data Science minor or Mathematics educational minor are allowed. Foreign study may include one 6 EC master unit that cannot be reused in a later master. Historical transition rules apply to earlier entrants rather than being stacked into this pathway.

core: Mathematics, computing and business analysis integrated to improve organizational decisions
Calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and mathematical optimization for business models
Programming, data management, machine learning and AI for organizational data
Business economics, finance and collaborative applications of analytics
adjacent: Advanced algorithms, computing and mathematical methods for optimization
Customer demand, pricing, finance and organizational strategy informed by analytics
Responsible decisions with business data and artificial intelligence
questions: How can organizations use data and models to improve resource allocation and decisions?
How can demand, pricing and consumer information shape business decisions?
How should organizations use AI and data responsibly?

alternatives.label: Business analytics across mathematics, data and organizations
alternatives.concept: Combines mathematical and statistical methods, programming, data science and AI with economic and business decisions. It approximates VU’s integrated field through UCR courses while lacking its continuous specialist projects and full operations-research sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial quantitative, computational and business study; no one strand alone defines it.
progression: All actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings verified; probability/statistics now precedes machine learning. Introductory mathematics precedes linear algebra/numerical methods/algorithms. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the final selected spring; the valid Linear Systems placement remains earlier without inventing an extra prerequisite.

alternatives.label: Algorithms, AI and mathematical optimization
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on formal and computational methods for business-related decisions, with deeper software development, systems mathematics and reinforcement learning. Business foundations remain as the application setting, while the curriculum gives less room to marketing and organizational study.
alternatives.labelReason: Advanced computing, mathematics and AI occupy the curricular differences from the integrated route.
alternatives.distinctness: Four course choices replace business AI, consumer engagement, market research and one advanced algorithms course with software development, linear systems, advanced calculus and reinforcement learning; the remaining technical courses still form a methodological concentration.
progression: All actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings verified; probability/statistics now precedes machine learning. Introductory mathematics precedes linear algebra/numerical methods/algorithms. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the final selected spring; the valid Linear Systems placement remains earlier without inventing an extra prerequisite.

alternatives.label: Data-informed markets, finance and strategy
alternatives.concept: Uses quantitative and data foundations to study demand, pricing, customer engagement, finance and digital business strategy. It gives organizational applications greater weight than the integrated route and does not claim the VU depth in optimization or advanced software.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set has a substantive business and market sequence supported by data and quantitative methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change from the integrated route: consumer economics, international business governance, applied finance and digital strategy replace advanced AI optimization, computational methods and algorithms. It differs even more strongly from the technical route.
progression: All actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings verified; probability/statistics now precedes machine learning. Introductory mathematics precedes linear algebra/numerical methods/algorithms. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the final selected spring; the valid Linear Systems placement remains earlier without inventing an extra prerequisite.

candidates.label: Market demand, pricing and business strategy

selection.assessment: The integrated mathematics–computing–business curriculum is the closest feasible UCR response. A deeper algorithmic route and a market/finance strategy route are separately evidenced and differ from each other and from the first route by at least four courses. Responsible AI is recorded as a further target-specific direction, but the three-alternative maximum is reached.

notes.text: VU Business Analytics requires a substantial sequence in calculus, operations research, statistics, programming and applied projects, including a 12-EC collaborative capstone; its third-year 30 EC elective period remains open. UCR combines related quantitative, computing and business courses, but does not reproduce that full specialist sequence or the VU project structure.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Business Analytics integrates mathematics, statistics, programming and AI to model organizational problems, optimize decisions and implement solutions through a compulsory sequence of applied projects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified directions: integrated business analytics; algorithms and mathematical optimization; and data-informed markets, finance and strategy. Each combines substantial quantitative/computational study with business questions. The business-focused option places greater weight on organizational applications. UCR does not reproduce VU’s full calculus, stochastic modelling, operations-research and business-project sequence, or its compulsory collaborative capstone. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed180 EC.
